title: The Corner Shop
story: Rosa stopped at the corner shop on her way home because there was no milk and no bread in the flat. The shop was narrow, and the shelves were full. Luis, the owner, looked up from the counter and smiled at her. Rosa took a wire basket and checked the list in her hand. She chose milk, eggs, tomatoes, and a loaf of bread. Near the window, oranges sat in a wooden crate, so she picked four ripe ones. A boy next to her stood on his toes and still could not reach a tin of beans. Rosa lifted the tin down and put it in his hands. At the counter Luis entered each price on the till and turned the screen so Rosa could see the total. She opened her purse and found that she was short. Her cheeks grew warm, and she reached for the oranges to put them back. Luis said she could take the food home and bring the rest of the money the next day. Rosa did not like to owe money, but the fridge at home was empty. She agreed and wrote her name and the amount in a notebook by the till. The next evening she returned with the coins and a little card. Luis smiled and pinned the card to the board above the counter. He said trust between neighbours kept a small shop alive.
